About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the role

Ramp Stack brings AI to the accounting work that happens after the transaction: reconciliations, prepaids and amortization, fixed assets, payroll entries, accruals, allocations, and variance analysis. Stack prepares reviewable work so the customer's team keeps accounting judgment and approval.

As a Stack Account Executive, you'll sell to finance and accounting leaders (Controllers, VPs of Accounting, CFOs) in a new, fast-moving product motion. You'll hear how a team actually closes the books, find the recurring manual step that creates drag, and turn it into a focused proof path and a commercial plan. This is broader than a month-end close pitch: you'll connect Stack to the finance team's goals for cleaner data, fewer handoffs, faster close, and more confidence in reporting.

What you'll do

  • Own the full sales cycle from first conversation to signed contract: discovery, tailored demo or scoped pilot, business case, negotiation, close.

  • Run workflow-level discovery: identify the recurring task, its inputs, the preparer and reviewer, and the cost of keeping it manual.

  • Scope and run pilots against a baseline and a success metric, then convert them into a mutual action plan and a decision.

  • Run a high-ownership, high-velocity motion (10–15 deals a month discussed as the lower band; quota target to confirm).

  • Combine Stack with Ramp's core products where it genuinely improves the data, control, or handoff behind the workflow.

  • Bring field feedback to Product, Marketing, and Enablement while the motion is still being built.

What you need

  • Quota-carrying, full-cycle closing experience selling to finance or accounting buyers (years of experience to confirm).

  • Exposure to accounting workflows (for example from Basis, FloQast, NetSuite, or similar reporting, forecasting, or close tools).

  • Comfort with a high-ownership, high-velocity motion in an early product.

  • Proven high agency: you build your own pipeline and process without waiting for a playbook.

  • Ability to discuss close, reconciliation, and reporting workflows credibly with Controllers and CFOs.

  • Daily, practical use of AI in your own work.

Nice to have

  • CPA, or an accounting or finance background, even earlier in your career.

  • An accounting-to-sales transition, or relationship-manager experience with sales, negotiation, and upsell or cross-sell.

  • Experience on a NetSuite incubation team or with a reporting or forecasting tool.

Job Description: Account Manager

We are seeking a highly analytical, execution-driven professional to join our global Account Management team. Comprising 80% core account management responsibilities and 20% project and business management focus, this role acts as an operational orchestrator sitting at the intersection of Front Office Sales, Risk & Governance, and external institutional counterparties.

You will own the end-to-end client lifecycle, complex multi-exchange DMA setups, periodic regulatory refreshes, and high-stakes reverse due diligence. Location: Bengaluru, India

  • Manage a high-volume pipeline of institutional KYB and HNI onboardings across multiple global legal entities.
  • Coordinate sequential onboarding handoffs across third-party exchanges, managing subaccount provisioning and continuous liaison between stakeholders and external exchange teams.
  • Drive ongoing periodic regulatory reviews under strict audit timelines, managing document collation, gap analysis, and timely escalations to Compliance

At Tenderly, we're not just shaping the future of blockchain technology – we're defining it. As a full-stack Web3 infrastructure platform, we provide multi-network support and a comprehensive ecosystem that covers every aspect of the blockchain journey, from initial encounters to advanced Node solutions and serverless cloud compute functions.

 

Our mission is crystal clear: to empower developers worldwide to harness the full potential of blockchain technology for creating innovative products. With our robust Web3 infrastructure platform, we've already enabled tens of thousands of developers to work more efficiently with blockchain.

 

We thrive on tackling complex challenges head-on, crafting solutions that push the boundaries of what's possible in the blockchain world. From developing bespoke Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) implementations to designing proprietary storage layers optimized for our advanced blockchain node solutions, our team is at the forefront of industry innovation.

 

About the Role

We are looking for a proactive and detail-oriented Legal Associate to own the ongoing legal matters that keep our Serbian entity running smoothly day to day.

This is a hands-on role for a legal professional with a strong foundation in Serbian corporate and commercial law, practical experience drafting and reviewing contracts in English, and the ability to independently manage the company's everyday legal operations and compliance.

You will work closely with internal stakeholders, including finance, operations, HR, and our US entity, as well as external legal advisors, taking ownership of local legal matters while helping ensure that our processes remain compliant, efficient, and well-organized.

The role is ideal for someone looking to grow their in-house legal experience in a technology-driven environment.

 

What You’ll Do

Corporate & Day-to-Day Legal Operations

  • Act as the first point of contact for Serbian legal matters arising from the company’s everyday operations.

  • Manage corporate housekeeping for the Serbian entity: Business Registers Agency (APR) filings, changes of registered data, corporate decisions, powers of attorney, and corporate records.

  • Own and maintain the legal and compliance calendar, ensuring deadlines and statutory obligations are met.

  • Coordinate required filings, registrations, and other local regulatory documentation.

  • Manage administrative and legal processes related to R&D tax incentives and subsidies.

  • Support finance and operations on the legal side of banking, payments, office lease, insurance, and other operational matters.

  • Maintain organized legal records and documentation, ensuring accuracy and timely completion of legal tasks.

Commercial Contracts

  • Draft, review, and redline commercial contracts and agreements in English, including vendor, SaaS, client, NDA, and service agreements.

  • Identify legal risks and propose practical, business-orien/ted solutions.

  • Support contract management and ensure consistency across legal documentation.

  • Provide legal support to internal stakeholders on contractual matters.

Compliance & Data Privacy

  • Organize and manage software compliance programs.

  • Provide legal counsel and support on data privacy (Serbian Law on Personal Data Protection) and regulatory compliance matters.

  • Draft internal policies and procedures as needed and regularly monitor compliance.

Intellectual Property

  • Manage the legal aspects of the Company’s intellectual property assets, including trademarks, copyrights, patents, and brand names.

  • Coordinate IP registrations, renewals, and related administrative processes.

  • Liaise with external advisors as needed on IP-related matters.

Employment Support

  • Support the HR team on Serbian labor law matters as needed, including employment contracts, annexes, and terminations.

  • Keep the Company’s general acts and employment-related policies up to date and compliant.

  • Advise on occasional disciplinary or employee relations matters.

External Counsel & Cross-Entity Coordination

  • Coordinate with and manage external lawyers and law firms on matters requiring specialized expertise.

  • Prepare clear briefs, provide relevant context, and manage follow-ups with external advisors.

  • Coordinate and align legal matters with our US entity.

  • Support internal stakeholders across the business by preparing legal documents and providing legal assistance as needed.

 

About You

  • A degree in Law from a Serbian university.

  • 2–4 years of relevant legal experience, ideally in-house within a technology or IT company in Belgrade or Novi Sad.

  • Strong working knowledge of Serbian corporate and commercial law, with solid grounding in employment law.

  • Hands-on experience with corporate housekeeping, APR filings, and day-to-day compliance for a Serbian company.

  • Working experience with employment documentation (contracts, annexes, terminations, internal acts).

  • Demonstrated experience drafting and redlining commercial contracts in English. Strong written English is essential.

  • Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple deadlines and processes independently.

  • A proactive, solution-oriented mindset and willingness to take ownership.

  • Ability to work effectively with external legal counsel and internal stakeholders.

  • Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and a practical approach to legal matters.

  • Strong ability to use AI tools in day-to-day work


    We are also open to candidates coming from a law firm environment, particularly associates who have developed strong drafting skills, demonstrate initiative, and are motivated to transition into an in-house role.

    Prior experience in blockchain or Web3 is not required. During your first period, you will be onboarded into the industry and our products, learning the business context behind the legal work.

    What’s Not Part of This Role

    The role focuses on Serbian legal matters and the company’s day-to-day legal operations. US commercial negotiations, litigation strategy, tax structuring, and ESOP/M&A matters will remain handled by senior internal stakeholders or external legal counsel.

    Why This Role?

  • Opportunity to take ownership of a broad range of Serbian legal matters.

  • Structured onboarding into the blockchain industry, with time to learn the business during your first months.

  • Exposure to a dynamic technology business and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Opportunity to develop practical in-house legal expertise and grow professionally.

  • A role where initiative, sound judgment, and operational ownership make a meaningful difference.

Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.

We’re remote-first by design and operate with intelligence at the center of everything we do. At Block, you'll be challenged by some of the brightest, most creative minds in the industry and have the tools and autonomy to do the most meaningful work of your career. 

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Sales Compensation Operations Analyst to independently lead complex commissions administration across multiple plans and sales populations. You’ll own end-to-end commission cycles, resolve complex operational issues, and strengthen the controls and processes behind accurate, timely payments.

As a senior individual contributor, you’ll partner with Finance, Payroll, Sales Operations, HR, and technical teams to drive improvements, support approved plan changes, and develop the team’s operational expertise. This role owns the administration of approved sales compensation plans, not sales compensation plan design.

You Will

  • Independently own end-to-end commission cycles across multiple plans and sales populations, managing timelines, dependencies, approvals, and validated payment submissions to Payroll.
  • Interpret and apply approved plan rules for participant eligibility, quotas, sales crediting, effective dates, and adjustments; oversee accurate plan assignments and participant changes.
  • Own complex reconciliations across sales transactions, commission calculations, adjustments, and payment totals, resolving discrepancies before payment submission.
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex commission inquiries, explain calculations and outcomes clearly, and coordinate resolution within approved policies. Document exceptions and secure required approvals.
  • Design and strengthen operational controls, review procedures, and audit documentation to improve accuracy, consistency, and traceability.
  • Lead root-cause analysis of recurring issues and use operational reporting to prioritize improvements that reduce errors, manual work, and payment risk.
  • Lead operational readiness and user acceptance testing for approved plan, process, and system changes, partnering with technical teams to define requirements, validate results, and resolve issues.
  • Mentor teammates, guide complex cases, and improve shared procedures and training materials to strengthen team capability and consistency.

You Have

  • 5+ years of experience in sales compensation, commissions administration, or related operations.
  • Demonstrated experience in sales commissions administration, including independent ownership of complex payment cycles across multiple plans or sales populations.
  • Strong spreadsheet and analytical skills, including advanced formulas, lookups, pivot tables, and reconciliation of large datasets.
  • Ability to interpret complex compensation plan rules, investigate discrepancies, and distinguish routine administration decisions from exceptions requiring approval.
  • Experience developing operational controls, supporting audits, and leading process improvements through implementation.
  • Experience translating business requirements into test scenarios, validating results, and assessing readiness for plan, process, or system changes.
  • Strong cross-functional communication and influencing skills, including explaining sensitive payment issues and resolving competing priorities.
  • Sound judgment, discretion with confidential compensation information, and the ability to manage ambiguity while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.

Nice to Have

  • Experience administering incentive compensation platforms, such as Pigment, Xactly, CaptivateIQ, or Spiff.
  • SQL skills for querying, validating, and analyzing commission-related data.

Technologies We Use and Teach

  • Pigment for ICM/quota issuance, Salesforce as the system of record & end user UI in Looker.

Finance · Full time · In person, San Francisco · Reports to Head of Finance

You will build and run the numbers the founders use to make decisions at both companies. Story is project-based, with a budget and margin on every film and client. Wizard is a venture-backed startup where runway and hiring pace drive the plan. This is strategic finance at seed stage: high autonomy, direct access to the CEO, and work that changes what the company does next week.

  • The operating models for Story and Wizard: revenue, cost of sales, headcount plan, cash flow and scenarios, current with actuals.

  • The reporting rhythm: weekly finance tracker, monthly P&L and budget vs. actual, and the founder review.

  • Pricing and deals: margin checks on every new proposal and retainer before it goes out.

  • Board, investor and fundraise support: metrics, model outputs and data room.

YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

  • Take over the weekly tracker and monthly reporting package for both companies.

  • Rebuild the forecast so it re-runs from actuals in under a day.

  • Put every open client project on one budget vs. actual view, with margin by project.

  • Have 4 to 7 years in FP&A, strategic finance, banking or consulting, and have owned a three-statement model end to end.
